en: She could honk my horn all night long!
I'd totally let her pop my clutch!
My eyes locked on my girl, there in the driver's seat next to me.
Well, duh. I don't have a driver's license, either.
Hello! Welcome to Club SEGA. Can I help you with anything?
Can you restock the UFO Catcher?
Can I get you to restock the UFO Catcher?
Can ya restock the UFO Catcher for me?
Could you restock the UFO Catcher, please?
Of course! Give me one moment.
Thank you for waiting.
No, it's fine. Thanks.
Uh, no, nothing. Thanks.
Never mind.
Uh, no, I don't need anything.
Oh, sorry, no. I don't need anything.
If you need any assistance, we're here to help. Have fun!
Think you could change out the prizes in the UFO Catchers?
All right, here we are, sir! Please have an enjoyable time!
Okay, let's see what this is like.
All right, here we are! Hope you have a good time!
Let's see what happens.
Okay, let's check this place out.
Right, let's do this.
All right, let's give it a try.
Hey, you there. I know you...
(Shit! Looks like my cover's blown!)
You're that prison escapee, Saejima! Hold it right there!
(I should come back when I'm alone.)
Would you like to participate in a snowball fight?
I'm sorry, sir, but it costs 1,000 yen to enter. Please come back when you have the entry fee.
Please select a course.
I'll take your 1,000 yen entry fee, then.
Good luck to you!
Sorry, maybe some other time.
I see. We'll look forward to you joining us.

You may participate in a snowball fight by speaking to the receptionist.
Each game costs 1,000 yen to play.
The participants are ranked according to the points they earn during the regulation time, with the winner earning a prize.

Points are awarded and subtracted as follows:

Hit an enemy with a snowball (strike): +3 Pts
Get hit by a snowball (hit): -2 Pts

You cannot earn negative points. Scoring doubles in the final thirty seconds.
You may not make your own snowballs. Get your snowballs from the restocking points in the four corners of the playing field.
By winning battles, you can advance to more challenging courses. The tougher courses offer better prizes.
I'm so sorry, but we stopped accepting new entries for our snowball fights. We hope you'll stick around to watch and take in the festival.
Good try out there! Please take this consolation prize.
You got <Color:8>Carved Wooden Doll<Color:Default>.
We hope you'll participate again.
Congratulations! Here's your prize. You deserve it!
You got <Color:8>Toughness ZZ<Color:Default>.
You got <Color:8>Tauriner ++<Color:Default>.
We look forward to having you join us again.
(I should come back here when I'm alone.)
This sucks...

en: (He seems really down. I'll just let him be.)
Get your ugly mug outta my face.
(Hey, isn't that Sosuke?)
Hey, what's wrong? You seem kind of down.
Huh? Oh, hey, old man. It's nothing, I'm just kind of hungry.
You want to go get something to eat? Your treat, of course.
Huh? Okay...
How broke are you, old man? You're making me pay? That's just sad.
Er, well... Sorry.
Man, what a meal! Thanks for the treat, old man.
(So he really is going to stick me with the check. Too late to say no now.)
Phew... I was feeling kinda down, but now that my belly's full, I don't really care anymore.
Guess it's true what they say about simple minds. I don't know what was bothering you, but are you okay now?
It seems kinda silly, but remember that talk we had about being popular with the ladies?
Well, it's not like it's all about the ladies, but it's just...
I dunno, being admired... it just feels good, you know? What people think about you matters.
Yeah, I guess it does.
But growing up, no one ever really looked up to me. Nobody told me I was good at anything.
I guess that kind of thing bothers me a lot more than I thought it did.
But no biggie. I mean, if I worried about what everyone thought about me, I'd never get anything done.
Anyway, I'm done worrying about that crap for now.
I'll be back at the usual place any time you got some time to kill.
You're back. Want to do some training?
No, maybe later.
Yeah? Catch you later, then.
Sure, let's do this.
You're on!
Let's start with guarding, the most basic part of fighting.
It's good to keep your guard tight, but just doing that won't win you any fights.
If you want to win, try this move. It's called the Komaki Knock Back.
Knock back?
I'll use the move on you so you can remember how it's done.
If you beat me, that means you figured out what I was doing. After that, mastering the move will be a snap.
<Color:7>Heat Actions are not available<Color:Default> in training battles. Also, make sure you are fully prepared, as Sosuke is a threat to be reckoned with.
You ready?
Yeah, let's get started.
All right, then. Oh, before I forget...
This is a training session, so I'll let you hit me a little. But if you get carried away, I might get a little ticked off.
What kind of training is this?
Look, this isn't a dojo. I do things my own way out here.
This time, we'll focus on the most basic of the basics: evasion.
Think of it this way. You can't lose if your opponent never hits you.
Then again, you'll never win if you don't go on the offensive, either.
So if you can attack while evading, you'll be unstoppable. Pretty simple, huh?
Yeah. The old evade and strike, right?
Right. The Komaki Evade & Strike to be exact. It's the perfect combination of both evasion and attacking.
Of course, it has its drawbacks. You won't be able to attack at full power, since you're evading at the same time.
The idea is to evade and strike to create an opening, then follow up with more attacks.
I'll show you by using the technique on you. That's the best way to learn.
Okay, you ready?
All right, then. Oh, and like I said before...
You'll get ticked off if I hit you too much? It's not like I'm going to hold back.
Suit yourself. You're the one who's going to suffer if it comes to that.
But enough talking. Let's go!
Now let's go over a way to take advantage of the opening an opponent leaves when he attacks.
The idea is to break through the attacker's defenses by using the momentum of his attack against him.
And to do that, you use the Komaki Parry.
Timing's everything with this one. Get it wrong, and your opponent eats your lunch.
But the only way to learn is the hard way. And by hard, I mean painful.
You know the drill, old man.
And remember, try not to get too carried away.
Heh, no promises.
It's your funeral, old man. All right, let's start!
Like last time, this is another way to use the opening an opponent leaves when he attacks.
Even the best of the masters leave themselves exposed for just an instant as they attack.
That's when you use the Komaki Tiger Drop, a vicious move that seizes that opportunity.
The Tiger Drop...
If you've used it before, you'll know you only have a brief moment to pull it off.
Study your opponent's attacks so you'll know the perfect time to unleash it.
The Tiger Drop is not an easy move to pull off.
But for now, I'll be using it like crazy. Just remember that it takes years to master.
It's one of those high-risk, high-return moves. Always good to have one in your bag of tricks.
I won't be taking it quite as easy on you this time. I won't be going all out, either, of course.
Heh, save the excuses and just get to it.
I like your style, old man. Let's go!
This time, I'll teach you something more conceptual instead of a straight-up technique.
Conceptual?
Yeah, it's different from before where I just tell you about a move and how to use it.
I don't follow.
You're not that good at flexible thinking, are you?
Well, don't worry, buddy. I'm going to teach you anyway.
People have a way of tapping into unimaginable power when their back's against the wall. What if we were able to do that at will?
It would be a huge advantage.
The fact that you can use Komaki style moves shows that you've trained your soul, technique, and body.
That means you should be able to tap into this off-the-charts power when you're backed into a corner, just like me.
Off-the-charts power?
The best way to learn is by doing, so brace yourself. The kid gloves are coming off.
Remember, you have to be backed into a corner. Just let me take care of that. The rest is for you to figure out.
Finally, some real training.
It's all been totally real. Want to take this seriously, old man?
Right. Sorry.
Whatever, let's get going.
Okay, let's do this!
Okay, you passed the test.
Knock backs are really useful in creating opportunities to attack, especially against tough opponents.
I couldn't care less if you forgot what my gramps taught, but you better remember what you learned from me, old man.
You learned <Color:9>Komaki Knock Back<Color:Default>.
About that... I'm sensing you have a lot of hostility toward the elder Komaki.
It's not hostility. I admit the old coot's got good stuff.
But he's getting old. I'm on the way up, while he's on a one-way trip down.
That makes me better than him. Wait, I take that back. I'm better than him even without taking that stuff into account.
Arrogant, aren't you? Personally, I don't think your grandfather's lost much of his edge.
It doesn't matter how good you are. If you don't do anything with your skill, what's the point?
What're you getting at?
Heh. Enough talk for now.
We can continue this conversation next time. That is, if you can complete the training I assign you.
Come on, old man. That was just plain sad.
Let's pretend that didn't happen, okay? Come back when you're ready to be a winner.
Okay, good enough. You pass.
To use Evade & Strike right, you gotta be able to evade when needed, you know?
If all you're thinking about is landing a blow, you'll be in for a world of pain.
Yeah, I get it.
You learned <Color:9>Komaki Evade & Strike<Color:Default>.
But hey, you move pretty well for an old dude.
You don't look like you play sports. So what, did you bust some heads back in the day?
No comment.
Keeping your past a secret, old man? Aw, whatever. It's not like I really care.
Hey, do you know how Gramps is doing?
I haven't seen him in a long time, but the last time we met, he was doing fine.
Huh...
If you're so interested, why don't you just go see him yourself? He'll be at the Kamurocho dojo unless he's moved on.
A dojo in Kamurocho, huh? Figures.
That's exactly why that old geezer's no good.
Anyway, the point is, I'm stronger and better looking to boot.
Wait, what're we talking about now?
Relax, old man. You'll go bald sweating the details like that.
Come on back if you feel the need. Later.
Okay, that's that. Let's just say you passed.
You learned <Color:9>Komaki Parry<Color:Default>.
As cocky as ever, aren't you? You're bound to piss people off if you keep acting like that. That'll be your problem, though.
So you say, but with my overwhelming strength and good looks, you'd have to be a moron to pick a fight with me.
Good looks have nothing to do with it. But as long as we're on the subject, are you what passes for good looking these days?
You may have a decent face, but you're kind of scrawny. No one I'd want to count on, at least.
What? Oh, I get it.
You're stuck in the past, old man. You're in serious dinosaur country.
Let me fill you in. Girls don't go for big, bulky musclemen anymore.
They're into the more sensitive types and guys who are ripped but still thin. You know, like me.
Thin but ripped?
Can't blame you if you're behind the times. I mean, you're old, anyway. Suffice to say, I'm the kinda guy the ladies are into these days.
So you're saying you're popular with the ladies?
No, that's a different matter.
How so?
It just is.
I'm the type of guy that's in right now. Ladies go for guys like me.
Just, you know, not right at this exact moment.
What? Sorry, you lost me there.
Ladies should be all over me, but they're not.
Come on, relax. I don't know what you're talking about, but does it really matter?
Guess not.
(He looks really depressed all of a sudden. I hope he snaps out of it.)
You made it through. I guess you pass, then.
You learned <Color:9>Komaki Tiger Drop<Color:Default>.
Either I pass or I don't. What's to guess about it?
You really like to fuss over the details, huh?
Man, I really hope I don't end up a useless old geezer like you and my gramps.
What, are you worried about growing old at your age?
